title: bls12-381-g1-ecdlp: partial-coverage Cheon attack v13 (executed binary-gcd construction, consistently itemized scratch bounds, streaming comb)

claims.statement: For uniform s in [1,r), inputs T=[s]P0=A_1 and the auxiliary powers A_i=[s^i mod r]P0, i=1..n, on BLS12-381 G1 with n=2^20, the single-shot classical two-phase Cheon algorithm v13 in proof.md recovers s with success probability at least 0.39 using total work W(2^20) at most 2^123.836032 target-group-operation equivalents (time_log2 = 123.836032 = 1934938/15625), including runtime factorization of r-1 as a deterministic, hard-capped, counted Brent-Pollard rho construction on the fixed public input (the iteration cap is checked BEFORE each consumed batch so a completed cycle provably uses at most 2^17 iterations; a hard 12-cycle guard bounds the total; every gcd is an EXECUTED round-counted binary gcd - Stein's algorithm, implemented in the experiment in place of math.gcd and verified against it on 201 sampled pairs including (r-1, 254760293^2) - at <= 48 instructions per round (4-limb compare 10, conditional subtract 10, multiword trailing-zero elimination 12, multiword shift 10, control 6) and <= 512 rounds per call (each round strips >= 1 bit of a < 2^256 total; asserted per call; measured maximum 153), i.e. <= 24,576 instructions per gcd; joint worst case three bounded terms: main loop 12 x 2^17 x 1056 = 1,660,944,384 = 2^30.629357 instructions, batched gcds 12 x 2^10 x 24,576 = 301,989,888 = 2^28.169925, backtrack <= 128 steps per cycle x 25,088 = 38,535,168 = 2^25.199672, total 2,001,469,440 = 2^30.898412 instructions = 2^19.932628 units, plus <= 2^10.60 units of Miller-Rabin certification and <= 2^15.579 units of comb tables: preprocessing total <= 2^20.01 units inside the 2^21 budget; measured for the fixed input: 111,717 modular multiplications, 310 gcds, 9 cycles; no probabilistic model is used anywhere), generator and subgroup construction, three fixed-base comb tables, all baby and giant scalar multiplications (one 512-instruction mod-r multiplication each, sequential; comb point multiplications charged 64 units against the stated construction of 32 window additions, each exactly one reference batched-incomplete-affine operation by the cost model's definition with one Montgomery batched inversion per window layer per block, plus <= 304 instructions of addressing and control), the bottom-up merge sort of the baby array over an auxiliary buffer (117 passes; <= m*117 key compares at 15 instructions; <= m*118 record moves at 50 instructions including the possible final copy-back; <= 16 instructions per record of key preparation: <= 7671 instructions per baby, an upper bound asserted in the experiment), binary-search giant lookups (at most floor(log2 m)+1 = 117 probes worst case - the candidate range at most halves per probe, asserted per lookup - each <= 32 instructions: 2-word midpoint 6, pointer and record loads 4, six-limb key load/compare 12, parity bit 2, interval update + termination + branches 8), at most two window-start exponentiations, both BSGS phases, assembly, verification and output. The attack uses d=2^20 (largest divisor of r-1 not exceeding the scoring n) and reads only A_1 and A_d. The comb generation STREAMS: giant scalars are generated and consumed in blocks of 2^24 records (never materialized as an m-sized list), each block's accumulator array is allocated for exactly the block size, and each block's points are binary-searched immediately and discarded; live working storage is itemized at 304 bytes per record (scalars 32, accumulators 96, Montgomery prefix products 48, separately allocated inverse-output 48, pending entries 72, indices 8) and charged at <= 512 B/record x 2^24 = <= 2^33 bytes, stated consistently in every file of this submission; the toy executes this construction with the per-block live accumulator and scalar array lengths recorded and asserted (live_accs = live_scalars = 64 at toy scale, 5 blocks) and equality to plain double-and-add asserted in full for EVERY point (all babies and every giant of every trial). Every table record is keyed by (x, y mod 2), which uniquely determines an affine point on this odd-prime curve (the at most two points sharing an x have opposite y-parities), so a key match is an exact point match and k1 = (i + m1*j) mod N is exact with no sign ambiguity. Phase 1 solves s^d = eta^k1 by partial-coverage BSGS over a contiguous window of m blocks at a uniform offset with the coverage an exact per-offset integer statement including all wrap-around hits: block j covers exactly the m values {(m1*j + i) mod N : i < m}, consecutive arcs are disjoint, so every offset covers at least (m-1)m/N >= 0.4 - 2^-118 >= 0.39 k1 values - a fully deterministic statement with no probabilistic quantity anywhere in the claim; the closed form is crosschecked against an exhaustive every-offset brute force on five smaller parameter sets. Phase 2 recovers the order-2^20 component deterministically; s = zeta^(k1+tN) is verified by [s]P0 = T. Peak memory by phase: the global peak is the sort phase (m-entry main array plus m-entry merge buffer = 256*m = 2^124.767581 bytes); during streaming giant generation only the sorted baby table (128m) plus <= 2^33 bytes of itemized block scratch is live: strictly above 2^124.7675 bytes including comb tables, code and scratch (memory_log2_bytes = 124.8); preprocessing at most 2^21 units (preprocessing_log2 = 21.0) included; nonuniform advice 0 bytes. Sensitivity: 384-unit double-and-add everywhere still gives ~2^126.3. All preconditions, the executed capped factorization with the binary-gcd verification, the parity-key uniqueness, the per-offset minimum coverage (>= 39/100 in exact integers) and the closed-form crosschecks are verified at production parameters by experiment.py Part A; Part B demonstrates the complete two-phase attack on a 20-bit toy group with d=6, factoring n-1 with the same capped construction, running the streaming comb, the explicit merge sort and binary search, and asserting equality with plain double-and-add for every point: full coverage 200/200 exact recoveries, 0 wrong extractions; the declared partial mode 88/200 = 0.44 vs the exact wrap-inclusive expectation 0.4022613461525126, 0 wrong extractions.

experiments.purpose: Part A executes at full production BLS12-381 parameters the deterministic hard-capped, counted Brent-Pollard rho factorization construction charged in the proof (pre-batch-enforced 2^17-iteration cap, 12-cycle guard; measured 111,717 modular multiplications, 310 gcds at a measured maximum of 153 binary-gcd rounds, 9 cycles) and asserts the result equals the supplied factor list in both directions; it verifies the round-counted binary gcd against math.gcd on 201 sampled pairs including (r-1, 254760293^2); verifies 2^20 divides r-1; zeta=7 generates Z_r*; eta has exact order N=(r-1)/2^20; zeta_e has exact order 2^20; d-th powers lie in the order-N subgroup; computes the per-offset minimum coverage in exact integers (>= 39/100 for every offset); crosschecks the closed-form coverage bound against an exhaustive every-offset brute force on five smaller parameter sets; and samples the (x, y mod 2) key uniqueness property on negation pairs. Part B runs the complete two-phase Cheon attack on a toy prime-order group (20-bit, d=6 | n-1, factored by the same capped construction) with production-shaped sequential window giants, baby and giant point sets computed by the charged STREAMING layer-batched comb (giant scalars generated and consumed in blocks of 64, never materialized as an m-sized list; each block's accumulator array allocated for exactly 64 records with the live lengths recorded and asserted; each block's points searched immediately and discarded; one Montgomery batched inversion per window layer per block; equality with plain double-and-add asserted in full for every point), the parity-keyed sorted baby array built by the explicit merge sort (compare/move upper bounds asserted) and searched by the explicit binary search (probe budget asserted per lookup), a brute-forced exact wrap-inclusive coverage expectation, and every extraction checked against the true scalar, in partial mode (the claimed regime) or full-coverage control mode. Toy evidence is evidence at toy scope only.
